question: The background picture in Oil Ocean fills the console's background picture memory completely, right up to a hardware wall, so the parallax editor cannot add a single new moving band to it. Not even the smallest one. The wall is real and cannot be moved: the background tiles end exactly where the sprite table begins, and every last slot is holding a distinct piece of artwork with no duplicates, no blank tiles and no mirrored pairs left to reclaim. The tool that drew the current background was never told to leave any room, so it used all of it. The version of that tool used before it deliberately kept about a hundred slots back for animation, and that reservation is what got lost. Whether the background art gets redrawn to make room is an art call, and it is yours.

options.name: Animate background artwork that is already there
options.what: Parts of the background that are already drawn can be turned into moving bands. This works on the real level today and needs no picture memory at all, because nothing new is drawn. What you cannot do is add a new moving element, or move artwork somewhere it is not already sitting. The four empty band slots stay empty.
options.costs: No art work and no waiting. One check is still outstanding on my side: the end to end path has been proven with a band built by the code, not yet with one built by hand in the editor. That check is a queue item and about an hour.

options.name: Redraw the background with room kept back for animation
options.what: The art tool gets told to stop short of the wall and keep slots free. Every band slot then becomes usable for anything you want to put in it, and the two animated bands that the last art run wiped out can come back at the same time.
options.costs: The background picture loses roughly a quarter of its distinct detail, which is a thing you would see if you stopped and looked at the sky and the rig. It costs one art run plus your eyes on the result, and it is work on the engine side rather than mine.

recommend.because: It puts a moving background on screen without touching art you already approved, and it is the only one of the two that can start today. If you later decide to redraw and keep room back, adding bands from scratch starts working on its own and none of the work built so far is wasted. So this is not a road that has to be undone, it is the first half of the same road.

detail: aeon games/sonic4/data/editor_bg_override.json is at 448/448 tiles. tileSlotsRemaining 0, bandsRemaining 4. 448 = (0xB800-0x8000)/32 exactly; the SAT at $B800 is the wall, tile 449 sprays into it. Measured against aeon pin e087af9c: 448 distinct bitmaps, 0 flip-redundant pairs over orig/H/V/HV, 0 uniform-colour, no H- or V-symmetric tiles, so dedup/blank/flip reclaim are all exhausted. The lever is the generator, not dedup: png_to_bg_override.py has no --max-tiles and only refuses above the ceiling; the superseded forest_bg_gen.py reserved 108 tiles by construction. Current blob is the output of the run that destroyed the two authored bands (see ROADMAP items 14 and 24). insertBand refuses at every size under saturation; promote/demote leave tiles.length unchanged and function today (item 27). The outstanding UI-made-band composition check is item 29.

question: I have been told, second hand through another session, that you gave every lane standing permission to publish its own repository's work without asking each time. I have no record of you saying it to this lane, and my own notes say that when that is the case I should ask you again rather than treat a relay as your word. So I am holding two finished pieces of writing unpublished until you confirm it. Two other lanes are waiting on the same sentence.

options.name: Yes, publish this repository's work without asking
options.what: Finished work reaches the shared copy as soon as it is done and verified. Rewriting history that is already published, touching another lane's repository, and putting anything on the public site all stay off limits and would still come to you.
options.costs: You will see work appear that you did not wave through one piece at a time. You would be trusting the checks I run before publishing rather than reviewing each one.

options.name: No, ask me every time
options.what: Nothing is published until you say so, one batch at a time.
options.costs: A message to you per batch, and finished work sits unpublished in between. Two pieces are sitting that way right now, and the other lanes are in the same position.

recommend.because: The relay says you already chose this when it was put to you as one question for the whole suite, so this is most likely just getting your answer written down somewhere it counts. The parts that are actually hard to undo, rewriting published history and putting things on the public site, are excluded either way, so what you would be handing over is the routine half.

question: Nothing is running in this lane and I am waiting on your word before starting anything. The item at the front is a real bug in files already written: when an author sets how far a background drifts vertically, the editor writes a value the game cannot read. The game then does something that looks almost exactly like pinning the background in place, with a one pixel wobble each frame, which is why nobody has ever noticed it. Every background scene this editor has made so far carries it.

options.name: Fix the vertical background drift value
options.what: The editor starts writing values the game actually understands, the setting becomes a plain number box instead of a list of named choices, and one saved test scene that carries the bad value gets corrected.
options.costs: About half a day for one agent. It touches saved scene files, so it is the kind of thing that gets more awkward the longer it waits and more scenes exist.

options.name: Fix the panel that swallows its own buttons
options.what: Buttons sitting in a panel's title bar, like adding a layer or deleting a scene, currently also fold the panel shut when you click them.
options.costs: Around an hour. It is annoying rather than damaging, and it damages nothing that is saved.

options.name: Neither, stay parked
options.what: I keep the lane idle and pick nothing up.
options.costs: Nothing is spent. The drift bug keeps being written into every new scene in the meantime.

recommend.because: It is the only one of the three that is quietly writing something wrong into files you keep, so it is the only one that gets more expensive by waiting. The button bug is irritating but it never leaves a mark on anything saved, and it will still be an hour's work next week.
